objective: Proof and computation. (1) The heights lemma: given the port class, the merged face's single skip lies on a known arc, so the ports' heights are fixed; the heights consistent with the class are closed under rounded midpoints, so a point is frozen exactly when its height difference to the ports cannot vary. (2) The reduction lemma: across a 3-edge cut, a side holding neither the attachment point nor the gluing line acts as the point or line it replaced, so collapsing it leaves the transfer and creation unchanged; the faces-around-the-point law then holds in the reduced space, which explains the junction counterexample of FACE-CLAIM-20261103-001C. Check both on ladders, grids, grown spaces, tubes and ladder arms spliced onto grids.
status: Proved by STRIP-RELAY-20261103-001A-P001: the port class fixes the ports' heights (the merged face's skip lies on a known arc), and heights with fixed port values are closed under rounded midpoints, so a port pattern freezes exactly the points whose height difference to the ports cannot vary (488 of 488 frozen cases). Across a 3-edge cut, a side holding neither the attachment point nor the gluing line acts as the vertex it lost, so collapsing it leaves the transfer and creation unchanged (253,536 pipeline cases; 1,080 exact cases); in the reduced space every creating far line lies on a face around the point, which explains the junction counterexample of FACE-CLAIM-20261103-001C
title: Heights and reduction
